gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.start.body:
# What is this mod about?
- Monsters attack your base in big raids. You plant a Defense Beacon, build around it and protect it.
- Win a raid and you get prizes. Spend them to get stronger. Then a bigger raid comes. Repeat.
- On the way you get guns, ammo tables, a kitchen, a support cannon and more. Each has its own page in this book.
# Your first steps
- Step 1: Look in your pack. You already have a Defense Beacon, this book, a Recovery Shovel and a starter gun.
- Step 2: Choose where to plant the beacon. Read the red notes below first!
- Step 3: Right-click the ground with the beacon, read the screen, then press Plant beacon.
- Step 4: A short first raid starts AT ONCE. Hold your gun, keep your ammo handy and stay close to the beacon.
- Step 5: Win it. You earn a Weapon Platform and your campaign is rolling.

# Defense Beacon
- What it is: A glowing crystal in the heart of your base. There is one per world, in the Overworld, and the whole team shares it.
- You get: A protected zone to build in, raids to fight and prizes for every win.
- How it works: Right-click it to open its screen: Overview, Upgrades, Workshop Fabrication and Raid break. Settings and this Guide are in the header.
- How to unlock: You start with one in your pack.
- Careful: The beacon cannot be broken or moved. Only the Recovery Shovel removes it, and that RESETS the whole campaign: every upgrade, win and reward tier goes back to zero. Your buildings stay.
- Careful: So choose the spot well, and leave clear space around it (see Your base zone).
- Careful: Wild monsters can hit an exposed beacon too if they can see it from 24 blocks away. Cover it with solid blocks.

# Recovery Shovel
- What it is: A special iron shovel. It is also your remote control for the beacon.
- You get: The beacon's control panel from far away, a status display while you hold it, free moving of your support gear, and a way to push enemies back.
- How it works: Right-click the air to open the panel. Hit a monster to knock it back (it does no damage). Use it on your Support Platform or Cannon to pick it up. Use it on the beacon to pack the campaign up.
- How to unlock: You start with one. Lost it? Craft a new one at a crafting table: iron above and below, copper left and right, redstone in the middle.
- Careful: Using it on the beacon is the reset button. The game asks you to confirm first.

# Field Guide
- What it is: This book.
- You get: Answers while you play.
- How it works: Right-click it to open. Pick a page from the list, or use Back and Next or the arrow keys. Scroll with the mouse wheel.
- How to unlock: You start with one. Lost it? Craft paper and a copper ingot together.

# Starter gun
- What it is: A basic gun and some ammo, so you can fight the very first raid.
[pack] - You get: One FK15P flintlock and 64 round balls for it.
[standalone] - You get: The weakest gun in your installed gun packs and 64 matching rounds.
[pack] - How it works: The flintlock holds one round and reloads slowly. Press {reload} to reload.
[standalone] - How it works: Press {reload} to reload.
- How to unlock: You get it once, the first time you join the world.
- Careful: You only get one. Ammo you spend stays spent, so make your shots count.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.zone.body:
# Your base zone
- What it is: The area around the beacon that is yours. A moving cyan grid shows its edges, even above and below you.
- You get: A safe home for your kitchen, Exchange Shop and support gear. They can only be placed inside it. Weapon tables inside it also raise your base score.
- How it works: At first it reaches 8 blocks each way from the beacon. Core upgrades make it wider. Vertical upgrades make it taller.
- How to unlock: It appears the moment you plant the beacon.
- Careful: It is centred on the beacon and never moves unless the beacon does. Leave a clear 3 x 3 space, two blocks tall, around the beacon, or the biggest Core upgrade (Mk-4) cannot be built.
- Good to know: You can switch the grid off in Settings.

# Base score and rewards
- What it is: A grade for your base. The beacon looks at what you built inside the zone.
- You get: A better base earns better prizes after every raid (reward tier 0 to 10). Overview shows your score.
- How it works: Walls, roofs and rooms you place count. Extra points for mixed materials, details (stairs, slabs, fences, doors), lights, furniture (beds, bookshelves, barrels, chests, tables) and closed rooms you can use.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. Just build.
- Careful: A higher reward tier means bigger raids that come more often: about weekly at tier 0, down to every 2 days. You can hold them back in Raid control.
- Careful: Natural terrain gives nothing, and ore blocks are worth no more than plain blocks.

# Settings
- What it is: Three switches in the header of the beacon screen.
- You get: The cyan zone grid, the sky beam and a red box showing the part of the beacon enemies can actually hurt.
- How it works: Click a switch to turn it on or off. The beam is shared by the whole team.
- How to unlock: Always there.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.body:
# Raids
- What it is: Waves of monsters that march on your beacon to wreck it.
- You get: A cache of prizes and Ardent Energy for winning. Everything the raiders broke is put back.
- How it works: Raiders appear outside your zone, walk straight at the beacon and break through doors and walls. Each has a red "!" above its head. Kill every one to win. Any left alive start to glow after a minute.
- How to unlock: Plant the beacon. A short first raid starts at once. After that raids come at night: about once a week at reward tier 0, and more often as your tier goes up (down to every 2 days). The clock counts ACTIVE days, so it stops while nobody is online.
- Careful: If three defenders die near the beacon, the beacon loses health. If it is overrun you lose, and the damage stays until you repair it.
- Good to know: A raider that cannot cross lava, a chasm or a wide lake, or gets stuck, stands still for about 8 seconds beside a red gate, then steps out of a second red gate just outside your zone. You can shoot it while it waits. After three gates it gives up and leaves.
- Good to know: Raids have their own music near the beacon, and winning plays a fanfare. Turn it down with the game's Music volume.

# Warnings
- What it is: Messages that tell you a raid is coming.
- You get: Time to get home and get ready.
- How it works: Chat warns you about a day ahead, then every six hours, then once more when the raid is only waiting for night. Big banners show the start, each wave, VICTORY and DEFEAT. A red BEACON IS BEING ATTACKED warning reaches every player, in any dimension.
- How to unlock: Nothing to do. They are always on.

# Hard raids and bosses
- What it is: Every third raid is a hard raid: simply a stronger raid with a boss. It has nothing to do with how often raids come.
- You get: A bigger prize, with a bonus on top.
- How it works: 25%% more attackers, and a boss walks in with the final wave. Beating the boss pays 50%% more completion rewards.
- How to unlock: It happens by itself. Overview tells you when the next raid is a hard one.
- Careful: Get ready for these. The boss is much tougher than the rest.
[pack] - Good to know: The boss is a modded boss with a red boss bar. Beating it also gives bonus medical kits and grenades.
[standalone] - Good to know: Without boss mods the boss is a vanilla Ravager.

# Special raids
- What it is: From the fourth raid on, about half of all raids come with a twist.
- You get: A little extra Ardent Energy when you win one.
- How it works: Overview names the next raid after each raid ends. The four kinds are below.
- How to unlock: Automatic, from raid 4.
- Air Raid: flying mobs ignore walls. You need anti-air, not thicker walls.
- Paratroopers: heavy mobs drop in on red parachutes. Shoot them while they float.
- Siege: creepers blow holes in your walls and shooters fire through the holes.
- They Are Thousands: only zombies, in huge swarms. Bring lots of ammo.
- Careful: Check what is coming and build the right counter before it starts.

# Special Forces
- What it is: Soldiers with guns who join raids once your reward tier is 4 or more.
- You get: Loot. Their bodies can be looted for about ten minutes after they fall.
- How it works: You get a warning first. Get behind sandbags and shoot it out. You meet one soldier per wave at tiers 4 to 6, and heavy soldiers from tier 7.
- How to unlock: Automatic once you reach tier 4.
- Careful: They shoot back from far away. Stay behind cover.

# Trap learning
- What it is: Raiders get used to the same trap again and again.
- You get: A good reason to mix your defenses.
- How it works: Each trap type hurts in full during the first wave. After that raiders take 25%% less from it every wave, until it does nothing after four steps. Chat tells you when they adapt. It starts over with the next raid.
- How to unlock: Automatic.
- Careful: Raiders are protected from sunlight only. Flame arrows and fire traps still work, but do not rely on one kind of trap. Turrets, guns, your own projectiles and your support cannon never get weaker.

# Winning and losing
- Win: Everything the raiders broke is put back. Your prizes go to the beacon's reward chest.
- Lose: The beacon is switched off and the damage stays. Repair it from Overview (see Repair or pack up).
- Careful: Spent ammo, fuel and tool wear are never refunded, win or lose.

# Reward chest
- What it is: The beacon itself. It is the chest that holds your prizes.
- You get: A 54-slot chest for the whole team, so loot stays out of your pack.
- How it works: Press Reward chest in Overview. New prizes are put in each time you open it, and whatever does not fit waits in a queue.
- How to unlock: It is there as soon as the beacon is planted.
- Careful: If the beacon is ever destroyed, what is inside spills out. If you pack the campaign up with the shovel, unclaimed prizes are thrown away, so empty the chest first.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.detail:
- Ordinary enemies have bounded health and no armor. Specialists have light armor, and marked heavies are uncommon.
- Special Forces begin at reward tier 4. Solo tiers 4 to 6 send one soldier per wave; heavies start at tier 7. When warned, get behind sandbags for a shootout.
- Downed Special Forces count as defeated, and their bodies stay lootable for up to ten active minutes.
- Extra nearby Survival or Adventure defenders raise reinforcement counts by 65%% each, not enemy health. The count locks at each wave and shows in Overview. Alive-enemy limits are 24 solo and 48 in co-op. Spectators, Creative players and distant players do not count.
- Veteran victories add at most 30%% reinforcements, with no hidden health growth. Boss health adds 45%% per extra defender, up to four.
- Defeats still count toward the three-raid cadence. Scheduled raids arrive at night.
- The reward chest needs two adjacent ground-level blocks clear with headroom, at least three blocks from the beacon, inside the zone. Create the first one between raids. Its 54 slots keep supplies out of your inventory.
- Higher reward tiers shorten the next interval: 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, then 2 days.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.detail.st: - Standalone rewards use vanilla resources, Ammo Coins and healing potions. Installed tactical consumables can also appear.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.body:
# Raid level cap
- What it is: A dial from 0 to 10 that limits how hard raids can get.
- You get: Easier raids while you are still weak. The cap limits both the enemies and the prizes.
- How it works: Press Lower level or Raise level in the Raid break tab. Your base score and upgrades are not touched.
- How to unlock: Always there.
- Careful: The whole team shares this dial, and a low cap means smaller prizes.

# Start raid now
- What it is: Do not want to wait for night? Start the raid yourself.
- You get: A raid at the level shown, with its prizes, at a time you choose.
- How it works: Press Start raid now. The base is saved first. Any break you bought ends. Every third raid still has a boss.
- How to unlock: Always there.
- Careful: Once it starts you cannot take it back. Check that everyone is ready.

# Raid break
- What it is: Pay to push the next raid back.
- You get: Five days of peace per purchase, so you can go on long trips. Buy more and they add up.
- How it works: Open the Raid break tab and press Buy five active days. Each purchase costs more than the last. Only days when someone is online count.
- How to unlock: Always there. The price is shown on the button.
- Careful: Every break also makes your NEXT raid tougher and richer (up to 3 tiers higher, never above your cap). Wild monsters still attack an exposed beacon during a break.
[pack] - Break price: brass, precision mechanisms and gold.
[standalone] - Break price: copper, diamonds and gold.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.detail:
- Purchases add up to three bonus tiers within your chosen cap.
- The next started raid uses the bonus and resets the purchase price.
- Starting a raid saves a snapshot of the base first. Ambient enemies stay active during a break.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.upgrades.body:
# How upgrades work
- What it is: Permanent boosts for the whole base, in six branches.
- You get: A bigger zone, better prizes, a tougher beacon and more.
- How it works: Right-click the beacon and open Upgrades. Each card shows what you hold and what it costs. Press Buy. Do it near the beacon, between raids.
- How to unlock: The tab is always there. In Creative mode everything is free.
- Careful: Packing up the beacon with the shovel wipes every upgrade.
[pack] - Making the parts: JEI shows the Create recipes for each upgrade component. Make enough, carry them, then buy. Hover a material icon: {jei}
[standalone] - Paying: Upgrades cost Ardent Energy, which drops from hostile mobs and from every won raid.

# Core
- What it is: The beacon's own strength, Mk-1 to Mk-4.
- You get: A wider zone and a tougher beacon with every level.
- How it works: There are three Core upgrades. Each grows the zone and the beacon's health.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
- Careful: Mk-4 needs a clear 3 x 3 space, two blocks tall, around the beacon.

# Logistics
- What it is: Your supply lines. This is how you earn better prizes.
- You get: Each of its five levels adds one reward tier. A good base adds up to five more. Tier 10 is the top.
- How it works: A higher tier means bigger prizes after every raid.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
- Careful: A higher reward tier also makes raids bigger and brings them more often. Lower the cap in Raid control if you need a breather.

# Defense
- What it is: Armor for the beacon.
- You get: 15, 30, 45 and 60%% less damage to the beacon, in four levels.
- How it works: Everything that hits the beacon does less damage.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.

# Restoration
- What it is: A repair crew.
- You get: Faster rebuilding after a raid, and the beacon heals 5, 10, 15, 20 and then 25%% of its health after a victory.
- How it works: It works by itself once bought.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.

# Vertical zone
- What it is: A taller base zone.
- You get: More room above and below, up to 16 blocks down and 48 up.
- How it works: It only changes the height. The beacon's health and model stay the same.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.

# Reconnaissance
- What it is: A scout.
- You get: Attackers glow the moment they appear, so you can see them through walls. Normally they only glow after one minute.
- How it works: You buy it once and it stays on.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.repair.body:
# Repair
- What it is: The fix for a beacon that a raid switched off.
- You get: +250 health and the campaign restarts.
- How it works: Open the beacon, go to Overview and press Repair. The button shows the price.
- How to unlock: The button shows up when the beacon is switched off.
- Careful: Repairs never refund ammo or fuel you spent.
[pack] - Good to know: Park and disassemble moving Create contraptions before raids.

# Pack up and reset
- What it is: The way to stop the whole campaign.
- You get: One fresh Defense Beacon back, ready to plant somewhere else.
- How it works: Hold the Recovery Shovel near the beacon and use it on the beacon, or use Settings > Remove. Read the screen, then confirm.
- How to unlock: Always possible, but you need the shovel within 8 blocks.
- Careful: Raids stop and ALL upgrades, wins and reward tiers go back to zero. Unclaimed prizes are thrown away. Your buildings stay.
- Careful: This affects every player on the world. Talk to your team first.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.stations.body:
# Weapon Platform
- What it is: The gun shop. A big workbench for guns.
- You get: Any gun you have unlocked, made from materials. Search by name and filter by type and era.
- How it works: Open it with empty hands. Pick a gun, check the materials and press Craft.
- How to unlock: Win the first raid to claim yours. Buy more at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: Guns from later eras are locked until the table is upgraded. A locked gun shows what it needs.

# Ammo Platform
- What it is: The ammo shop. It only shows ammo that fits the gun in your hand.
- You get: Bullets and empty magazines.
- How it works: Hold your gun and right-click the table, or press {interact} while looking at it. Pick the ammo and pay with materials or with Ammo Coins.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: A magazine you craft here is EMPTY. Fill it with your loose rounds using the magazine addon. Coins buy empty magazines, never filled ones.

# Attachment Platform
- What it is: The attachment shop: scopes, grips, extended magazines and more. It only shows parts that fit the gun in your hand.
- You get: Upgrades for your gun.
- How it works: Hold your gun and right-click the table, or press {interact} while looking at it.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: Some parts need a later Age. The list counts how many are still locked.

# Armor Platform
- What it is: The armor shop: helmets, vests, leg protection, boots, pouches, plates and vision gear.
- You get: Protection and extra carrying room.
- How it works: Open it with empty hands.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.

# Workshop Fabrication
- What it is: A tab on the beacon that sells the starter version of every table and workstation.
- You get: The four tables, the kitchen blocks (Mess Hall, Cook Pot, Bowl Dispenser, Milk Dispenser), the Support Platform, the Support Cannon and the Exchange Shop. Eleven in all.
- How it works: Stand near your planted beacon, open the tab, find the card and press Make. The price comes out of your pack.
- How to unlock: Plant the beacon.
- Careful: Kitchen blocks, the Exchange Shop and support gear must be placed inside your zone.

# Ammo Coins
- What it is: A special coin you only win from raids.
- You get: Ammo without the materials. At the Ammo Platform, Buy with coins pays for the whole batch shown.
- How it works: Win coins, then spend them at the Ammo Platform.
- How to unlock: Complete raids. Coins cannot be crafted.
- Careful: The coin price grows with the Age and the strength of the gun.

# Supplies
- What it is: A category in the Weapon Platform: food, medical kits, grenades, tools and gear materials.
- You get: Everything that is not a gun, ammo or armor.
- How it works: Open the Weapon Platform and pick Supplies.
[pack] - How to unlock: Supplies follow your Create research. Simple field gear starts open. Medical kits and grenades need Workshop research, and advanced supplies need Precision research.
[standalone] - How to unlock: Everything starts open. Prices use plain vanilla materials.

# Ages
- What it is: Five levels each table can reach: Frontier, World Wars, Modern, Advanced and Exotic.
- You get: Newer guns, ammo, attachments and gear.
- How it works: Each of the four tables has its own Age. Open a table, pick the Upgrade tab and press the one big Upgrade button. A ladder shows where you are and what comes next, and the materials show what you hold.
- How to unlock: Every table starts at Frontier.
[pack] - Careful: Modern and later Ages need a team visit to the Nether and the Create precision parts.
[standalone] - Careful: Modern and later Ages need your team to visit the Nether.
- Careful: Age locks still apply in Survival. A modern pistol stays a Modern unlock.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.energy.body:
# Ardent Energy
- What it is: A glowing item you win by fighting. It is the money of your base.
[pack] - You get: It pays for flares, the Support Cannon and Exchange Shop goods.
[standalone] - You get: It pays for flares, the Support Cannon, Exchange Shop goods, beacon upgrades, repairs and Mess Hall upgrades.
[pack] - How it works: Hostile mobs drop it now and then (about one kill in fifteen). A boss always drops one. Every won raid pays a fixed amount, more at higher reward tiers.
[standalone] - How it works: Hostile mobs drop it now and then (about one kill in twelve). A boss always drops one. Every won raid pays a fixed amount, more at higher reward tiers.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. Go and fight. You cannot craft it.
- Careful: A kill needs a player or a raider behind it. Mobs that die on their own drop nothing.

# Exchange Shop
- What it is: A shop booth with two tabs, Sell and Buy.
- You get: Sell spare materials for Ardent Energy, or buy supplies with it.
- How it works: Hand in goods on Sell. Spend energy on Buy. Buying always costs more than selling the same thing, so you cannot loop it for profit.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, or craft it from copper, iron, glass and redstone. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: The offers come from a text file that server admins can change, so a server may sell different things.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.energy.detail:
- Base drop chance 6.67%% (8.7%% standalone), +1%% per Looting level. Raid attackers count too. Tune it in config/arsenal-beacon-common.toml.
- Offers are plain text in config/arsenal-beacon-exchange.txt, in a [sell] and a [buy] section: 'minecraft:diamond = 6' is one diamond for 6 energy, 'minecraft:arrow x16 = 3' is sixteen arrows. The pack lists Create parts and the standalone edition rare vanilla materials.
- The shop reads its file every time it opens, so edits apply without a restart.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.support.body:
# Support Platform
- What it is: Your own landing pad and supply box. Every player builds their own.
- You get: A place where your deliveries land and where your Return Flare brings you home.
- How it works: Fill its supply grid (3 x 3 at first, up to 6 x 6 as it levels up). It stays where you put it.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, or craft it. Place it inside your zone with the block in front of it clear.
- Careful: You can only have one, and only you can open it. It stops working while the beacon is gone.
- Careful: The two blocks in front of it are a no-build "KEEP RETURN ZONE CLEAR" spot. Keep them empty or your Return Flare cannot bring you home.
- Good to know: Move it for free with the Recovery Shovel. It keeps its level and contents.

# Support Cannon
- What it is: A big gun that belongs to you. Everything you call goes through it.
- You get: Supplies by parachute, a ride home and bombardments on your enemies.
- How it works: It turns toward your flare with a grinding of gears and fires once it has settled. It handles one call at a time. Click it to choose your fire support and buy upgrades.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform or at Workshop Fabrication, for Ardent Energy.
- Careful: One per player, and only the owner can use it. Place it anywhere inside the zone, as far from the platform as you like.

# Support Flare
- What it is: A flare that calls in supplies.
- You get: A chest with everything in your supply grid. It parachutes in outdoors, or appears at your feet underground.
- How it works: Fill the grid at your platform. Throw the flare where you want the supplies. The cannon fires, then the chest arrives. Chat counts the seconds.
- How to unlock: Buy flares at your Support Platform, in the Shop tab.
- Careful: The grid is emptied when the chest is sent, so refill it after every call. If something is missing you keep the flare and get a message.

# Return Flare
- What it is: A ticket home.
- You get: A purple portal that takes you to your Support Platform.
- How it works: Throw it. The cannon fires and a portal opens where the flare landed. Step in. Only you can use it, it works from any dimension, and it closes after 30 seconds.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform.
- Careful: It needs a free spot in front of your platform. If there is none, the flare is not used up.

# Fire Support Flare
- What it is: A flare that calls a bombardment.
- You get: Shells that land on enemies inside a red box.
- How it works: Throw it at enemies. The cannon shells the box with the fire support YOU chose. Hold the flare to see your choice above the hotbar. Throw a second one during a barrage and you see "Barrage in process": it waits its turn.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform.
- Careful: The Bunker Buster hurts every player inside its box for half their maximum health, whatever armor they wear. If its box touches your beacon zone, the flare is handed back.
- Good to know: Far from your cannon? Chat says "Cannon preparing" when it starts to turn and "You heard cannon fire roaring" when it shoots.
- Good to know: The cannon fires up into the sky. Listen for the whistle: the shells drop straight down onto the flare, through rock if they must.

# Fire support types
- Explosion Barrage: shells that explode on the target.
- Arrow Cluster Bomb: a rain of arrows, with 2 more volleys.
- Narukami's Favor: lightning on every hostile mob, with 1 fewer volley.
- Bunker Buster: one huge bomb that digs out everything in its box.
- Healing Barrage: heals players inside.
- Curse of Debilitation: puts the worst debuffs on hostile mobs.
- Cluster Strike: bomblets all over a much wider area, with 1 fewer volley.
- Cryo Shell: freezes hostile mobs almost in place, with 2 fewer volleys.
- Napalm Carpet: leaves the ground burning; mobs in it keep getting hurt. 2 fewer volleys.
- Gravity Well: drags hostile mobs together, then crushes them. 3 fewer volleys.
- Shockwave: throws hostile mobs away from the flare, off your walls. 2 fewer volleys.
- Starshell: one light in the sky for 30 seconds. Hostile mobs glow and you see in the dark.

# Cannon upgrades
- What it is: Ten upgrades you buy by clicking your cannon.
- You get: Faster turning, faster fire, more shells, more damage, a wider area, reach underground, a longer-lasting portal, a healing aura, a slowing field and fire support in other dimensions.
[pack] - How it works: Click your cannon, open the upgrades and buy with factory parts. The Reference tab lists the prices.
[standalone] - How it works: Click your cannon, open the upgrades and buy with Ardent Energy. The Reference tab lists the prices.
- How to unlock: Buy the cannon first.
- Careful: Without Quantum tunneling, a fire support flare that lands underground is handed back. Without Dimensional link it does not work in other dimensions.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.support.detail:
- Prices at the platform: Support Flare 3 energy, Return Flare 2, Fire Support Flare 6, Support Cannon 12. The Exchange Shop and the Support Platform are also sold in the beacon’s Workshop Fabrication tab for iron, copper, redstone and glass.
- Supplies arrive 12 seconds after the cannon fires for a flare that landed outdoors, or 7 seconds underground. Chat counts the seconds down. The time the cannon spends turning comes on top.
- The cannon is heavy: it spins up and brakes slowly, so a flare behind it takes longer to answer. It can only work on one call at a time.
- Fire Support lasts 12 seconds (6 shells). Each shell takes 1.5 seconds to fall from the sky. Each shell deals 25 damage to hostile mobs touching the red box (within 4 blocks of the flare) and never hurts players or breaks blocks.
- The Bunker Buster is the exception: its box reaches 8 blocks down as well as up and sideways, every block inside it is dug out (the Defense Beacon, base blocks and super hard blocks such as obsidian, crying obsidian and bedrock are spared), and it hurts every player inside for half their maximum health, whatever armor they wear. If its box touches your beacon zone the flare is handed back.
- The portal stays open for 30 seconds and only its owner can use it. It works from any dimension.
- Parcels disappear after 30 minutes and drop what is left inside.
- Upgrades Mk-2, Mk-3 and Mk-4 cost 16, 32 and 64 reinforced plating and grow the grid to 4 x 4, 5 x 5 and 6 x 6.
- Only the owner can open their platform or cannon.
- Each Area of effect level widens the area by 1.5 blocks each way.
- Cluster Strike: each shell bursts 6 blocks up into 6 bomblets spread over an area 1.75 times as wide; each bomblet deals 15 damage within 2.5 blocks, and a mob is hit by one bomblet per shell at most.
- Cryo Shell: 8 damage, then hostile mobs are nearly stopped for 5 seconds (a raid boss for half as long).
- Napalm Carpet: each shell leaves its box burning for 5 seconds. Mobs inside take 5 damage a second and burn.
- Gravity Well: hostile mobs in the box, and up to 3 blocks beyond it, are dragged to the flare for 3 seconds. Then the well collapses for 20 damage. A raid boss is barely moved.
- Shockwave: 12 damage and a strong push away from the flare. A raid boss is barely moved.
- Starshell: one light that burns 30 seconds. Hostile mobs within 16 blocks glow, and players there see in the dark. Each Area of effect level adds 2 blocks.
- Each volley level adds 2 shells and each damage level adds 25 percent. Rate of fire cuts the gap between shells from 40 ticks to 33, 26 and 20.
- Without Quantum tunneling a fire support flare that lands below ground is handed back. Supply and return flares are not affected.
- Dimensional link lets fire support flares work in the Nether, the End and other dimensions (the cannon still needs your base to stand). Supply and return flares are not affected.
- The Lasting portal stays open for 5 minutes and works twice: once home, once back to where you threw it.
- The Healing aura circles a supply flare (6 blocks) and ends 30 seconds after the parcel is emptied.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.kitchen.body:
# Mess Hall
- What it is: Your kitchen counter. You put food on it and it cooks meals that boost you.
- You get: Sandwiches you carry with you, and big pots of stew for the whole team.
- How it works: Open it. Buttons that do things are on the left; the effects you can choose are on the right. Click the effects you want, press Gather ingredients and the hall lays out the right food from your pack, then press Make sandwich or Cook stew.
- How to unlock: Craft one from planks, a furnace, iron and a barrel, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: Gather ingredients spends nothing. Cooking does. Choose no recipes and the hall picks effects from whatever food you put on the table.

# Sandwich
- What it is: A meal you carry in your pack.
- You get: One or two effects, usable anywhere. They stack up to 16.
- How it works: Put one bread in the Base slot and two or three different foods in the other slots, then press Make sandwich.
- How to unlock: Every Mess Hall makes them, even a Mk I.
- Careful: The bread in the Base slot never gives an effect. Only the fillings do.

# Cook Pot and stew
- What it is: A pot that holds a big batch of stew for many people.
- You get: Up to three effects and 5 to 9 servings, depending on your hall's level.
- How it works: Put the pot within 8 blocks of the hall and pick it on the hall screen, then press Cook stew. Right-click the full pot with a bowl to eat. A board on the pot shows the effects and the servings left.
- How to unlock: Your Mess Hall must be Mk II or better. Craft the pot from iron, a sign and a cauldron, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: A Mk I hall cannot cook stew. Cooking into a pot that still has stew asks you first, and the old stew is thrown away. A cook that cannot work spends nothing.

# What a meal does
- What it is: Food buffs. They show as ordinary potion effects, plus a "Home Zone" effect.
- You get: More health, armor, speed, damage and luck, plus gun boosts like faster reload and less recoil.
- How it works: A meal lasts 15, 20, 25 or 30 minutes in the field, longer from a higher level hall. At home, inside your zone, every value is DOUBLE and the timer stops. Logging out pauses it too.
- How to unlock: Just eat one.
- Careful: Dying clears your meal. Milk clears it too. A new meal replaces the old one.

# Mess Hall levels
- What it is: Four levels of hall, Mk I to Mk IV. Each one adds something.
- You get: Mk I: sandwiches only. Meals last 15 minutes. 3 food slots.
- Mk II: unlocks stew. Meals last 20 minutes.
- Mk III: meals last 25 minutes. Unlocks ×2 doubling (see below).
- Mk IV: meals last 30 minutes. Opens all 6 food slots.
- How it works: Open the hall and press Upgrade to Mk N on the left. It lights up when you can afford it. Hover it to see what the next level gives.
[pack] - How to unlock: Pay 8, 16 and 32 Reinforced Beacon Plating.
[standalone] - How to unlock: Pay 4, 8 and 14 Ardent Energy.
- Careful: Your food and pot links stay when you upgrade. Creative mode is free.

# Doubling (×2)
- What it is: A way to make one effect count twice.
- You get: That effect is twice as strong. Its card in your order shows ×2.
- How it works: Put two DIFFERENT foods of the same type on the table that both give the effect, for example cooked chicken and cooked mutton for Vitality. One food is not enough, and two stacks of the same food do not count. Gather does it for you when your pack allows.
- How to unlock: Upgrade the hall to Mk III.
- Careful: A legendary effect needs two different foods from EACH of its two groups. That is four food slots, so only a Mk IV hall can double one.

# Bowl Dispenser
- What it is: A box of bowls for eating stew.
- You get: A bowl with one right-click. A message tells you how many are left.
- How it works: To stock it, crouch with BOTH hands empty and right-click. Put up to 64 bowls inside. Bowls come back when you eat, so one stack goes a long way.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: It cannot make bowls. When it is empty it only tells you so. Breaking it drops its bowls.

# Milk Dispenser and Milk Bottle
- What it is: A tank of milk that cleans you.
- You get: Right-click and every effect on you is cleared.
- How it works: Each use takes 250 mB from an 8,000 mB tank. Refill it with milk buckets (1,000 mB) or Milk Bottles (250 mB): crouch with empty hands and right-click to open it. A message tells you what it cleared.
- How to unlock: Buy the dispenser at Workshop Fabrication. Craft 4 Milk Bottles from a milk bucket and 4 glass bottles (you keep the bucket).
- Careful: It clears EVERYTHING, good effects and your meal too. If you have nothing to clear it says so and spends nothing.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.mixes.body:
# Legendary meals
- What it is: Special meals that help you handle guns.
- You get: Small bonuses while the meal lasts: damage, reload speed, recoil, accuracy and more.
- How it works: Each one needs foods from TWO specific food groups (list below). In the Mess Hall click its icon in the second row and press Gather ingredients.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. All fifteen are open once you have a Mess Hall and the right foods.
- Careful: A legendary meal uses up BOTH of its food groups, so those groups cannot also feed everyday effects. Two legendary picks cannot share a group.

# The fifteen mixes
- Protein + Grain: Firepower (+8%% gun damage in the field)
- Fruit + Grain: Quick Hands (+10%% reload speed)
- Protein + Fungi: Brawler (+20%% gun bash damage)
- Protein + Vegetables: Heavy Hand (+15%% gun bash knockback)
- Fish + Fungi: Demolition (+10%% grenade and rocket radius)
- Vegetables + Grain: Recoil Control (−10%% recoil)
- Fish + Vegetables: Focus (+10%% aimed and hip-fire accuracy)
- Fish + Fruit: Snap Aim (+10%% aiming speed)
- Fruit + Fungi: Fast Draw (+10%% draw speed)
- Protein + Fish: Dead Eye (+8%% headshot damage)
- Protein + Fruit: Gun Mobility (+8%% gun movement-speed multiplier)
- Fish + Grain: Impact (+0.25 bullet knockback)
- Vegetables + Fruit: Rapid Fire (+5%% rate of fire)
- Vegetables + Fungi: Scoped Focus (+15%% aimed accuracy)
- Grain + Fungi: Hip Focus (+15%% hip-fire accuracy)
~ A Mk IV hall can double a legendary effect: two different foods from each of its groups (four food slots). At home every value doubles again. Six different groups, which needs all six food slots, make three legendary effects at once.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.mixes.detail:
# Everyday ×2 pairs (Mk III and up)
- Vitality: cooked chicken + cooked mutton.
- Fortitude: carrot + potato.
- Steadiness: brown mushroom + red mushroom (bread + wheat also works).
- Mobility: cooked cod + cooked salmon.
- Might: raw beef + cooked beef.
- Agility: cookie + pumpkin pie.
- Fortune: apple + glow berries.
- Recovery: honey bottle + golden apple.
- Hearth: rotten flesh + spider eye.
- Springy Step: chorus fruit + melon slice.
- Swim: raw cod + raw salmon.
~ Apple also feeds Fortune and melon also feeds Springy Step. Hover any recipe icon to see every food that feeds it.
# Food groups
- Protein & dairy: raw and cooked land meat, egg, milk, rabbit stew.
- Fish: raw and cooked fish, pufferfish.
- Vegetables: carrot, potato, beetroot, beetroot soup, dried kelp, golden carrot.
- Fruit & sweets: apples, berries, melon, sugar, honey, golden apples, chorus.
- Grain: bread, wheat, baked potato, cookie, pumpkin pie.
- Fungi & fermented: mushrooms, mushroom and suspicious stew, rotten flesh, spider eye, poisonous potato.
~ Each food belongs to one group and each distinct item counts once. A legendary recipe reserves BOTH its groups; other groups can still feed everyday effects you choose.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.upgrades.detail:
- Logistics: five levels add five reward tiers. Building adds up to five more, for tier 10 at most. Better tiers shorten raid intervals down to two days.
- Defense: 15 / 30 / 45 / 60%% less beacon damage. Restoration: 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25%% maximum-HP healing after victory.
- Creative mode purchases and upgrades are free.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.gear.body:
# Gun Guide
- What it is: A small card on your screen that lists the controls of the gun in your hand. It is its own mod and only runs on your computer.
- You get: Your real keys for Fire, Aim, Reload, Fire mode, Melee, Inspect, Attachments and more. A warning if two actions share one key. A red JAM alert when your gun jams.
- How it works: Draw a gun and the card opens for five seconds, then shrinks to a small badge. Press its key to open or hide it. Change the key in Controls, under Create Arsenal Gun Guide.
- How to unlock: Install the Gun Guide mod. There is nothing to craft.
- Careful: The JAM alert only works with the TaCZ Durability addon. Without it the controls card still works.

# Gun Displays
- What it is: Eleven decoration blocks for showing off guns: stands, wall racks and glass cases. Some are wide, some are made for pistols and one is for heavy weapons.
- You get: A trophy room for your best guns.
- How it works: Right-click with a gun to put it on display. Right-click with another gun to swap. Right-click with empty hands to take it back.
- How to unlock: Install the Gun Displays mod. With the Defense Beacon installed, get them from the Weapon Platform's Supplies category instead of the crafting table.
- Careful: Wall racks need a solid wall behind every part. Glass cases show guns smaller so magazines clear the glass.
